auxiliary_source_passages.statement_original:
We now introduce the energy levels of the process $(X_t)$. For a scale $j\ge2$, a location parameter $k<2^{j-1}$ and an averaging index $p\ge0$, we define
\[
d_{j,k,p}=\frac1{2^{j/2+p}}\sum_{l=0}^{2^p-1}\left(X_{(k+l2^{-p})2^{-j}}-2X_{(k+1+l2^{-p})2^{-j}}+X_{(k+2+l2^{-p})2^{-j}}\right)
\]
and
\[
Q_{j,p}=\sum_{k=0}^{2^{j-1}-1}(d_{j,k,p})^2.
\]
Note that the last sum stops at index $k=2^{j-1}-1$ and is defined only for $j\ge2$ because our observations stop at time 1.

Fix $j\ge0$ and $p\ge0$. For $0\le k<2^p$, we introduce the pre-averaged local energy levels of the log-integrated-volatility as follows:
\[
d_{j,k,p}=2^{-p-j/2}\sum_{l=0}^{2^p-1}\left(\log\left(\int_{(k+1)2^{-j}+l2^{-j-p}}^{(k+1)2^{-j}+(l+1)2^{-j-p}}\sigma_u^2\,du\right)-\log\left(\int_{k2^{-j}+l2^{-j-p}}^{k2^{-j}+(l+1)2^{-j-p}}\sigma_u^2\,du\right)\right).
\]
The corresponding energy levels are obtained via
\[
Q_{j,p}=\sum_{k<2^{j-1}}(d_{j,k,p})^2.
\]

First, notice that for a fixed $(j,p)$ such that $j+p\le N$, the price increment $S_{k2^{-j}+(l+1)2^{-j-p}}-S_{k2^{-j}+l2^{-j-p}}$ is $\mathcal A^n$-measurable and
\[
\left((S_{(l+1)2^{-j-p}}-S_{l2^{-j-p}})^2\right)_{l\ge0}=\left(\int_{l2^{-j-p}}^{(l+1)2^{-j-p}}\sigma_u^2\,du\ \xi_{j,p,l}^2\right)_{l\ge0}\tag{11}
\]
holds in distribution, where the $(\xi_{j,p,l})_l$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian variables, independent of the volatility process $(\sigma_t)_t$.

\]

To that end, for $S>0$, $\nu>0$ and $I>0$, we define

statement_resolution.shared: Brownian motion, fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H, independence, Ito integration, Gaussian laws, variance, expectation, probability, sigma-algebras, measurability, compactness, extrema, factorials, finite sums, Lebesgue integration, dyadic powers, floor, convergence and tightness are ambient. The paper names fractional Brownian motion without a separate main-text covariance-normalization definition; no external reference is expanded. D1 and D2 preserve independent price and volatility drivers. Price observations on [0,1] are distinct from observing volatility. D3 describes the observation vector parametrically; D5 and D7 supply the two different laws and domains. The notation n=2^N comes from page 5 and is reused in the general construction; the general experiment does not inherit a positive coarse mesh delta. Latent targets A1/A2 and representation A3/A4 are auxiliary source context rather than extra dependencies needed to compute the explicit observed statistics.
statement_resolution.2: D5 fixes the piecewise-constant model, original compact D with nonempty interior, observation sigma-algebra A^n and law P_H,eta. D4 supplies the mesh delta and integer block size, and D6 resolves lower rate of convergence. The theorem binds v_n(H) and w_n(H). The eta version changes the estimation target in the same probability minimax definition. The maxima preserve two separate regimes; the log n multiplier is only in the n-dependent eta branch.
statement_resolution.3: D5 supplies the experiment, D4 the mesh and dyadic regime, and D12 the estimator and positive threshold nu_0. D12 resolves through the estimated energies D11, empirical second differences D10 and observed log-block variables/noise law D9. The theorem binds kappa_0(H)=4-2^(2H); this is not the general-model kappa_{p,1}. The rate is bound in the statement and the tight family uses v_n^-1 without repeating (H). Uniform tightness is over the original D. The threshold has a strict upper bound and positive lower restriction from the preceding construction. Latent coefficients in A1 explain the target but are not required to evaluate the displayed estimator.
statement_resolution.4: D7 supplies the continuous model and compact subset of (0,3/4)x(0,infinity); D8 gives the corresponding lower-rate criterion. The theorem binds both rates. No delta, block noise, coarse estimator, truncation S or general upper-bound estimator is needed to state this lower bound.
statement_resolution.11: D7 supplies the general experiment, D13 the coordinate extrema, and D24 the recursively defined estimators and integer iteration count. The estimator closure uses D19-D20 observed first-difference energy estimates, D21 initialization and frozen hat j_n, D22 additional bias correction, D23 corrected maps, and D18/D17 the original bias and kappa functions. D15-D16 resolve all Gaussian integrals and overlined summation indices inside kappa, and D14 fixes integer expansion order S. A2 gives the latent target and implicit k range, A3/A4 give the coefficient-error context, and A5 records the generic correction domain. The stopping condition inside the theorem includes m_opt>m as well as the lower bound for every interior H; no m is silently removed. Rate functions are bound in the theorem. source_issues: The verified source is arXiv:2210.01214v2 dated 15 February 2024, 61 pages. Register version/URL strings are aliases for these same bytes. Original versioned source identity is preserved.

Main-text references finish above the Appendix A heading on page 56. Appendix bodies and their theorem statements are excluded. Four actual main-text Theorems are 2,3,4,11; numbering gaps are other result types.

Experiments in Sections 2 and 3 have the same observable grid but different volatility laws and parameter domains. The general-model H<3/4 restriction is not replaced with the broader extension discussed in Section 4.
The source normalizes sigma_0^2=1 in Section 2 and sigma_0=1 in Section 3. Driver independence rules out a leverage effect; the companion paper is outside scope.

The minimax criterion is a liminf of infimum over all data-measurable estimators followed by supremum over parameters. It is not a pointwise lower bound or an expected-loss definition. Rate dependence on H is preserved.
Delta appears as delta_n in the block observations and as delta in the model and rates. The source permits a sequence but does not separately spell out every limiting regime in the theorem bodies.

Page 5 defines n=2^N and m=n delta integer. Page 7 indexes block observations below delta_n^-1, but its empirical coefficient indices use 2^(N-j). Their compatibility for arbitrary m is unresolved; no automatic redefinition of N is made.

The coarse estimator on page 8 uses log, whereas the general estimator uses log_2. The coarse original is preserved; its intended logarithm base and the claimed consistency need clarification rather than silent correction.
Equation (5), not needed to evaluate the retained coarse estimator, contains an extra 2^-j in its middle noise subscript. It is not used to repair or redefine the empirical coefficient formula.

Coarse scale selection explicitly ranges from 2 to N-1 and returns 2 on an empty set. The general selections omit both the range and the empty-set fallback; these are not transferred without evidence.

Both constructions can encounter nonpositive noise-corrected energy estimates. The source does not fully define off-event logarithm, ratio, square-root and empty-maximum conventions. Clamping the eventual value does not itself define these intermediate operations.

The general latent definition states k<2^p but its Q sum uses k<2^(j-1). General empirical expressions also permute j,p,k in d and e, and the estimated Q sum leaves the k range implicit. Exact originals and auxiliary target context are retained.
The noise correction is 6 Var(bar epsilon_m)2^(-j-p) in the coarse model versus 2^(-j-p+1) Var(log xi^2) in the general model. Hat d^2 denotes an estimate of a square, not a squared estimate.

The initial general estimates are projected to the bounding rectangle, which need not equal the compact D. The scale hat j_n depends on the initial H estimate and remains fixed in later eta corrections.

The iteration is sequential: the mth eta update uses H^(m) and eta^(m-1), not H^(m-1). The theorem retains the extra intermediate m in m_opt>m>1/(4H)-2H-1, although the preceding construction only states the weaker m_opt inequality.
The truncation S is an integer constrained by both S>=1/(4H_-)+1/2 and S>H_+/(2H_-)-1/2. It is not the price process S_t, and it is distinct from iteration m and block length m reused elsewhere.

The Gaussian-integral definition uses an uncentered W for total degree b=1 and increments for b>=2. Factorials and the distinction between plain fractional Brownian W and fraktur integral W are preserved.

The overlined sum on page 31 restricts multi-index entries to {1,...,S}, whereas the preceding W and g definitions use {1,...,2S}. Equation (36) retains the stated overlined-sum convention; its truncation dependence is not simplified.

Kappa_{p,a} is available in main-text equation (36), even though it is inside a proof section. Its W-integral and index definitions are included because the estimator consumes them. Isserlis expansion, remainder Z, H-star and surrounding proof lemmas are not extra statement dependencies.

The bias function has argument order (I,nu), with sum starting at a=2. Lemma 10 later reverses parameter names in its displayed arguments; this proof-bound formula is not used to change the estimator definition.

Theorem 11 is boundedness in probability uniformly over D, not a central limit theorem or moment-risk bound. Theorem 3 similarly asserts uniform tightness, without distributional or expected-error conclusions.

Appendix C supplies a trigamma expression and moment bound for the coarse noise, but the noise distribution itself is defined in the main text. The census uses that distribution to resolve its variance and does not import an appendix formula.
